parts.title: SPIRAL REVIEW (5 min)
content: 1. GRAMMAR SPIRAL (Caption Writing): Write correct captions for: a) A bar chart showing temperatures in 4 cities. b) A pie chart showing types of plastic in the ocean. c) A line graph showing dolphin population over 10 years. Format: 'Figure [N]: [description]'
2. MATH SPIRAL: From your research data, choose 3 statistics. Decide: which chart type is most appropriate for each? (bar chart / line graph / pie chart) Explain why.
3. VOCABULARY: What is the difference between: a) chart and diagram? b) caption and label? c) legend and title? Give one example of each.

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Visual aids make a presentation more engaging and help the audience understand complex information. Research shows that people remember 65% of information they hear AND see together, compared to only 10% of information they hear alone.
content: 📖 Visual aids make a presentation more engaging and help the audience understand complex information. Research shows that people remember 65% of information they hear AND see together, compared to only 10% of information they hear alone.

There are several types of visual aids for a research presentation. A POSTER displays key information on a large sheet — it should have: a clear title, headings, bullet points (NOT full paragraphs), images or diagrams, and data charts. PRESENTATION SLIDES (like PowerPoint) should follow the '5-5-5 rule': no more than 5 words per line, 5 lines per slide, 5 text slides in a row (then an image). A DATA CHART or GRAPH makes statistics easy to understand visually.

Good visual aids SUPPORT the speaker — they do not replace them. The audience should be listening to YOU, not just reading your poster. Keep text minimal. Use images and data to make complex information simple.
(↑ Re-read the story above to answer:)
